strings: Deathguard Linnea is a Forsaken soldier stationed at a Deathguard waystation in southeastern Tirisfal Glades. She helps secure the roads between Brill and the eastern borders, watching for threats posed by the Scarlet Crusade and lingering Scourge. Adventurers passing along the main thoroughfares often assist her unit with patrol duties.

Deathguard Linnea stands sentinel at a small fortified post southeast of Brill. Life—or unlife—on patrol in Tirisfal Glades is treacherous, as the Forsaken must vigilantly defend their fledgling realm against Scarlet Crusade infiltrators and mindless Scourge prowling the wilderness. Stationed alongside her fellow guards, Linnea oversees patrol efforts along the roadway, coordinating reports with local authorities such as Magistrate Sevren in Brill to keep the realm's southern approach secure.

Tarren Mill serves as the Horde's primary outpost in the region, facing immediate pressure from Alliance outposts like Southshore as well as savage local wildlife. Samsa's duties involve securing the perimeter and directing capable adventurers to eliminate threats before they endanger the encampment.

The Deathstalkers serve as Lady Sylvanas Windrunner's eyes, ears, and blades across Lordaeron. When sent to scout northern Silverpine Forest, Rane and her brother Quinn found themselves hemmed in by surrounding feral dangers, turning an undercover reconnaissance mission into a battle for survival.

Holed up inside a derelict farmhouse at the Ivar Patch, Rane Yorick finds her mission compromised. The ghoul Ivar the Foul has badly mauled her brother Quinn, and worgs roam the fields between her and the safety of the Sepulcher. Deathstalker Vincent was a Forsaken scout sent alongside Deathstalker Adamant to infiltrate Shadowfang Keep. Slain by the mad mage Arugal, his corpse remains inside the stronghold as a grim warning to any who challenge the feral worgen within.

Before the Forsaken could launch a full-scale assault against the beasts holding Shadowfang Keep, intelligence on the fortress's interior was desperately needed. Two operatives from the Deathstalkers, the intelligence arm of the Forsaken, slipped past the barricades: Vincent and Adamant. Their mission ended in disaster. While Adamant was captured and locked away in a dungeon cell, Vincent was dragged directly before Shadowfang's master. Refusing to bend the knee or serve Arugal's dark designs, Vincent was executed on the spot, his body discarded on the stone floor to rot as a testament to the mage's fury.

Arugal used Vincent's demise to issue a scathing declaration to the intruders in his keep. Confronting the captive operative, the mad mage mocked the Forsaken and compared their intrusion to the failed efforts of his former Kirin Tor comrades. Demanding that Vincent surrender his blade and secrets to his master, Arugal struck the scout down when he refused, declaring that Vincent's moldering remains would serve as a warning to anyone foolish enough to trespass in his domain.

Deathwing the Destroyer, once known as Neltharion the Earth-Warder, is the fallen Dragon Aspect of the black dragonflight. Driven mad by the dark whispers of the Old Gods, he turned against the other Aspects and plunged the world into fire and turmoil. Though defeated near Grim Batol after the Second War and believed slain or hidden away, the terror of his legacy still haunts the deep places of Azeroth.

Before he was known as the Destroyer, Neltharion was granted dominion over the earth and the subterranean vaults of Azeroth by the titan pantheon. Yet dwelling so close to the world's deepest chambers exposed him to the insidious whispers of the imprisoned Old Gods. During the ancient War of the Ancients, the madness took complete hold. He deceived the other Dragon Aspects into imbuing a golden disc, the Dragon Soul, with portions of their essence under the guise of halting the Burning Legion, only to turn the terrible weapon against his allies and unleash catastrophic devastation.

Following the Second War, Deathwing sought to tear down mortal kingdoms from within. Taking the human identity of Lord Daval Prestor, a charismatic noble, he charmed King Terenas Menethil II and the high council of the Alliance of Lordaeron, plotting to install himself on the vacant throne of Alterac. Meanwhile, he aided the Dragonmaw clan at Grim Batol to keep Queen Alexstrasza enslaved while harvesting her clutches. His machinations unraveled when the four other Dragon Aspects rallied against him, shattering the Demon Soul.

In the present year, the mortal kingdoms largely assume Deathwing was destroyed or permanently driven from the world. However, the black dragonflight remains an active scourge across Azeroth. Led by his cunning brood, including his daughter Onyxia and son Nefarian, black drakes manipulate the politics of mortals and terrorize the landscape from mountain lairs. The scars of the black Aspect's ancient treachery run deep, and travelers wandering through craggy wastelands and deep subterranean tunnels still fear the stirring of the Great Dragon.

Deathwing was originally Neltharion the Earth-Warder, the leader of the black dragonflight empowered by the titans to shepherd the land and mountains of Azeroth. Millennia ago, proximity to the deep earth made him vulnerable to the insidious whispers of the Old Gods, eroding his sanity.

Deino is a Darkspear troll mage trainer dwelling within the Valley of Spirits in Orgrimmar. Alongside her fellow practitioners, she teaches emerging arcanists how to master the arcane and harness volatile elemental forces. She also directs seasoned spellcasters across Kalimdor to unravel ancient magical anomalies and seek out reclusive tutors.

Standing amidst the totems, huts, and tranquil waters of the Valley of Spirits, Deino offers instruction to Horde mages who find themselves in the orcish capital. Troll spellcasters traditionally walk a fine line between spiritual reverence and pure arcane mastery, and Deino represents this unique path within the Darkspear tribe, standing shoulder to shoulder with fellow instructors Enyo and Pephredo.

Beyond fundamental spell craft, Deino tasks promising spellcasters with field research far beyond Durotar's red dust. She sends practitioners northward into the corrupted wilds of Ashenvale to gather the tainted Waters of Xavian and recover enchanted hair from the Laughing Sisters. When a student's power outgrows what Orgrimmar can offer, Deino points them toward remote masters, such as the hermit sorceress Tabetha in the swamplands of Dustwallow.

Delgren the Purifier is a human paladin stationed at Maestra's Post on the northern edge of Ashenvale. Operating alongside comrades Balthule Shadowstrike and Feero Ironhand, he aids the night elves in cleansing demonic and shadow magic threatening the frontier, with a particular focus on the sinister Cult of the Dark Strand.
A Crusader on the Kaldorei Frontier

Human paladins are a rare sight deep within the ancient forests of Kalimdor, but Delgren the Purifier arrived with a mission. Affiliated with the Argent Dawn, Delgren traveled west with a cadre of holy warriors determined to assist the Alliance's new night elf allies against the lingering evils of demons and undead remnants from the Third War. Stationed near the border of Darkshore and Ashenvale, he maintains a watchful vigil over travelers passing south from Auberdine.

Delgren's immediate crusade pits him directly against the Cult of the Dark Strand, a malevolent cabal operating around the Tower of Althalaxx in northern Darkshore. Teaming with the scout Balthule Shadowstrike, Delgren orchestrates strikes into the cult's territory, investigating their dark rituals and sending adventurers to strike down cultists, shatter their summoning focuses, and root out corrupt warlocks who dare traffic with demonic shadow.

Despite his fierce devotion to the Holy Light and zealous nickname, Delgren possesses an unusual perspective on Kalimdor's tangled politics. Much to the annoyance and disdain of his conservative superiors, he took the time to learn Orcish. This rare linguistic skill hints at an unconventional mind—one that seeks to understand the enemies and neighbors sharing this untamed continent rather than relying solely on blind dogma.

Demisette Cloyce is a human warlock trainer sequestered in the subterranean crypts beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind's Mage Quarter. Operating under cover of the city's underbelly, she instructs practitioners of the fel arts and directs promising acolytes toward deeper, more dangerous arcane mysteries.
The Crypts of the Slaughtered Lamb

While Stormwind's authorities maintain an outward veneer of order and holy righteousness, practitioners of fel magic convene in the dank cellars beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in the Mage Quarter. Demisette Cloyce makes her residence down within these catacombs, tutoring warlocks willing to brave the forbidden arts. She holds little patience for the untrained or the uninitiated, advising her students that the dark energies corrupt only those lacking the discipline to master them.

Demisette is far more than a simple spell tutor; she serves as an essential nexus for warlock operations across Azeroth. When an acolyte reaches sufficient mastery, she directs them far beyond the walls of Stormwind—connecting them to powerful summoners like Menara Voidrender in the Barrens to harness potent artifacts and bind formidable fel steeds.

Denalan is an accomplished night elf herbalist and botanist who tends a quiet lakeside plot along the eastern shore of Lake Al'Ameth. Working under a simple awning, he devotes his days to studying the island's plant life and seeking botanical remedies for the strange corruption affecting Teldrassil. He frequently enlists young adventurers to gather samples, study violent timberlings, and test enchanted soils.

While many kaldorei focus on martial vigilance or high druidic rites, Denalan pursues the patient, meticulous craft of herbalism. Stationed along the tranquil eastern banks of Lake Al'Ameth, he has established a modest research camp consisting of a cloth awning, simple field tools, and tidy rows of cultivated planter boxes. Rather than retreating to the grand barrows of Darnassus, he prefers to remain close to the loam, directly examining the unusual flora that has sprouted since the planting of the new World Tree.

Denalan's research is far more than an academic curiosity; it addresses the growing unrest among Teldrassil's native wildlife. The timberlings, normally docile woodland beings of wood and sprout, have turned increasingly aggressive. Denalan enchants specialized soil to nurse wild seeds in captivity and analyze how malignant forces seep into the root systems. By studying strange specimens like shimmering fronds, glowing fruit, and moss-twined growths, he seeks to isolate whatever dark taint is troubling the forest boughs.
